Looking at the cuboid (3×2×2 = 12 cubes), the black piece occupies the three bottom-front cubes plus the top-middle-front cube (a T-shape), and is fully visible.

The visible white cubes are the top-left-front, top-left-back, and top-middle-back cubes — an L of three cubes in the top layer. The visible gray cubes are the top-right-front and top-right-back cubes.

The three hidden cubes (bottom layer, back row) must be split: two to gray (to complete its 4 cubes) and one to white. For the gray piece to stay connected, it must take the hidden cubes at back-right and back-middle-bottom, forming a zigzag piece. That leaves the hidden back-left-bottom cube for the white piece, attaching underneath the corner of the white L.

So the white (unshaded) piece is a central cube with three arms at right angles (front, side, down) — the "corner" shape, which matches option C.
